newsitem.title: GERMANY: German debt and futures stumble in late dealings.
newsitem.headline: German debt and futures stumble in late dealings.

text.p: German Bunds and futures stumbled in late dealings, hurt by comments from French Prime Minister Lionel Jospin, fresh U.S. economic data and the failure of September Bund futures to break a key chart point.
DTB September Bund futures fell about 60 basis points after the contract reached a key chart resistance point at 101.58 points but failed to gain momentum to keep going higher.
The Philadelphia Fed report pressured U.S. and German debt markets after it showed a business activity index in June of 25.2 compared with 1.6 in May, adding to the losses.
Another factor weighing on the market was Jospin saying the public finance situation was "serious" but that he was committed to European monetary union starting on time in 1999.
"The Philly Fed index gave the market a kick but the market before that was looking to be in a weak condition from a technical standpoint," said one Frankfurt trader.

September Bund futures ended trade down 32 basis points at 101.01 and near the session low at 100.94 reached when paring early gains, some of which were tied to the west German Ifo business climate index rising to 95.3 from 94.7 percent in May.
A deal between German Finance Minister Theo Waigel and Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer over the valuation of currency reserves at the central bank had little impact.

"The market has noted what happened but that's about it," said one trader. "We are tracking very closely with south European markets over EMU worries and that was the case over worries about Jospin's speech."
Traders voiced pessimism about the outlook, saying September futures must reach 102.00 points to keep the upward trend intact and to fend off a test of 100.50.
